# `silk/bench/html`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Draws a benchmark report as one static HTML page with charts.

## When to use
Call [`Html.page`](#Html.impl.page) on a `silk.bench.record.Report` to make a page you can open, attach to a
pull request, or publish. `silk.bench.bench` calls it for the outputs a suite declares with
`Format.Html`, and for `--html`.

## Details
The page is one file: its style is inline, its charts are inline SVG, and it loads nothing
and runs no script, so it opens the same from a disk, an archive, or a web server. It follows
the reader's light or dark color scheme.

Each benchmark has the table of `silk.bench.render` and one chart on a shared time axis that
starts at zero. A row of the chart is an implementation: a bar to its median, a whisker over
the 95% interval of the median, and one dot for each run, so a reader sees the spread and
any outlier. A bar is green or red only when the verdict is `faster` or `slower`; the table
says the same in words.

Import as `Html` with `import silk.bench.html { Html }`.
